header.title: Equities can absorb above-target inflation and higher yields while earnings hold

s01_bottom_line.text: The article documents that the S&P 500 sits less than 2% below all-time highs despite hot CPI/PPI prints and two-decade-high long-end yields, that equities historically compounded through long above-2% inflation regimes, and that consensus still calls for ~30% S&P 500 EPS growth. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate; approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩

As long as earnings hold, equities can take hotter inflation and higher yields; if guidance shows weaker demand, margin pressure or rising financing costs, the same inflation data will matter much more. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩

The article's investable view is that inflation and yield levels matter little for equities until they show up in earnings; the research opportunity is to watch earnings and credit transmission rather than inflation prints alone, since a targeted above-2% regime is historically survivable.
